ai_summary: Great Britain is currently recording a total GB wind output of 5.5 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 2.6 GW, which accounts for 25.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Thanks to this regional renewable dispatch, Scottish carbon intensity has plunged to a remarkable 4 gCO2/kWh, sitting in stark contrast to the 186 gCO2/kWh recorded GB-wide. However, persistent cross-border transmission limits prevent this clean electricity from reaching demand centers further south. Consequently, 15.6 GWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring an immediate constraint cost of about £632,186. To compensate for this stranded green energy, thermal generation was dispatched elsewhere, burning an estimated 2,968,142 m3 of gas and releasing an extra 5,468 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Extrapolating these constraint expenses yields an estimated total yearly cost of £231 million. Recovered through broad system charges, this curtailment penalty adds an estimated £1/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK. Accelerating transmission infrastructure upgrades remains vital to resolve these bottlenecks, curtail consumer costs, and halt the unnecessary burning of fossil fuels.
